Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-16T16:00:00Z
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Vong (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (PivotWise Product), Tobias Reed (PivotWise Eng Mgr), Lina Gomez (PivotWise ML), Ravi Kapoor (PivotWise Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be fuzzy): POC kickoff to map traffic profile. Customer expects short high-intensity checkout spikes. Need replay + synthetic benchmarks, measure p99 and cost.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, uh thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, i'll hand off to priya in a sec to go over the technical framing but quick agenda line - align on workload signature, success criteria, and the benchmark plan, sound good?
[00:22] Maya Chen: yeah thanks, real quick we have a hard launch coming Q4 so we're trying to validate infra for checkout flow, main ask is: can we sustain spikes where traffic goes from 80 QPS to 1,400 QPS for 20-40 seconds without p99 blowouts.
[00:40] Priya Patel: okay that's helpful, couple clarifying q's - is that 1,400 sustained or aggregated across regions? and what's the typical request size in tokens?
[00:55] Lina Gomez: most requests are short, avg input about 35 tokens, output averages 160 but there's a long tail — like 10% of requests produce 400+ tokens for receipts and followups.
[01:10] Tobias Reed: and those big outputs correlate with post-purchase upsell generator, rare but high token count and they tend to come in same bursts.
[01:20] Priya Patel: got it. So we need both QPS/concurrency sizing and token distribution for per-token compute. For modelling i'd recommend hitting three regimes: steady-state (50-120 QPS), moderate bursts (400-600 QPS for 2-5 min) and micro-bursts (1k-1.5k QPS for 20-40s).
[01:42] Ravi Kapoor: that micro-burst is the scary one for infra, our limits right now are 5Gbps egress per AZ but we can raise if needed with cloud ops, depends on pilot window.
[01:53] Jordan Lee: quick note - when you say p99 we interpret as end-to-end (including network) or just model inference? need to align on SLO measurement point.
[02:05] Maya Chen: p99 is end-to-end from request received by our edge to response returned to user. We prefer to keep p99 below 350ms for the checkout happy path, we can tolerate higher for upsell flows but it still needs to be within 800ms.
[02:22] Marcus Vong: okay that means we'll measure both inference-only and end-to-end in the benchmark. We'll instrument synthetic and replay so we can attribute latency.
[02:33] Priya Patel: question on model family — are you planning to use a 70B style model or a smaller 13/14B? that changes cost and batching behaviour a lot.
[02:45] Lina Gomez: current prod is tuned to an open 13B fine-tuned policy, but we're evaluating a 33-70B retokenized generator for quality on upsell. For checkout we can keep 13B. So POC should test both families as compatible variants.
[03:02] Jordan Lee: perfect. For the pilot we usually recommend two model variants: primary (13B quantized) and fallback (33B/70B with aggressive batching disabled) so we can test graceful degradation.
[03:15] Tobias Reed: curious about KV cache and prefix caching — can that handle the 400 token context we have for some invoices?
[03:25] Priya Patel: yes, our runtime supports kv cache and prefix caching, but cache hit rates vary; we'll want to capture prefix reuse from your sampled trace dataset. If hit rates are high, effective throughput improves.
[03:37] Maya Chen: about data residency and audit logs — we need SOC2 evidence and an audit log for every tokenized request. Is that in the standard POC?
[03:48] Jordan Lee: yes we can provide access to security docs and we can enable detailed audit logs in the private pilot environment. We'll attach the SOC2 package and an example log format.
[03:58] Priya Patel: moving to benchmarking, suggested plan: 1) replay of anonymized production trace (48h window) 2) synthetic stress with controlled bursts 3) tail-latency micro-bursts to model cold starts and scale-up. We'll measure p50/p95/p99, cost per 1M tokens, and model throughput in tokens/sec per GPU.
[04:20] Lina Gomez: for replay we will strip any PII, how do you ingest sample? s3 link or direct upload?
[04:28] Jordan Lee: s3 link is easiest, encrypted with customer KMS — we can provide a presigned upload and the replay harness will run inside our test VPC or your VPC depending on comfort.
[04:38] Ravi Kapoor: for security we prefer the replay run inside our VPC for the pilot, do you support VPC peered private deployments for short-term tests?
[04:46] Priya Patel: yes, we support a private pilot with a limited control plane handshake and VPC peering. There's a short onboarding step to open ports and set up IAM role. We'll document it in the runbook.
[04:58] Marcus Vong: on metrics, we'll also output batching statistics: avg batch size, batch latency contribution to p99, and KV cache hit ratio, plus the breakdown of tokenization buckets so you can see the 10% heavy tail.
[05:12] Tobias Reed: what's the expected GPU footprint for the 1.5k micro-burst? if we need to hit that in region with low latency, cost becomes material.
[05:22] Priya Patel: rough napkin calc: for a 13B quantized variant we can serve about 300-400 concurrent small requests per A100-like instance under aggressive batching. For 1.4k QPS you'll need multiple replicas + autoscale behavior to hit the micro-burst headroom. We'll size conservatively in the proposal.
[05:40] Lina Gomez: can you provide a sample cost delta between hosted and a dedicated reserved pool for our baseline?
[05:47] Jordan Lee: yes, we'll send a delta: hosted pay-as-you-go, dedicated reserved capacity gives lower unit cost but requires commit. We'll include a 3-month and 12-month reserve scenario in the cost sheet.
[05:58] Maya Chen: i want to call out success criteria: 1) p99 end-to-end < 350ms for checkout path during moderate bursts, 2) graceful fallback for heavy token responses with p99 < 800ms, 3) cost per 1M tokens within 20% of our target, and 4) no data exfil concerns during pilot.
[06:21] Jordan Lee: noted. We'll put those as the primary acceptance criteria in the pilot doc.
[06:28] Priya Patel: timeline suggestion: day 0-3 prep, day 4-10 baseline replay and instrument, week 2 synthetic burst testing, week 3-4 soak and parameter tuning, decision week 6. Does that match your internal timeline?
[06:43] Tobias Reed: yes that fits our Q4 window, we may compress if we can get the sample fast.
[06:50] Ravi Kapoor: small note — we have a maintenance window on 09/29 where peering changes are limited; coordinate pilot peering before that.
[07:00] Jordan Lee: we'll flag that date.
[07:05] Priya Patel: technical deep dive — how we model request concurrency: the replay harness will preserve arrival timestamps; we also produce a synthetic injector that can shape bursts with Poisson vs fixed-window bursts so we can see worst-case queuing.
[07:23] Lina Gomez: do you simulate network jitter? some of our 3rd party latency is variable and affects end-to-end p99.
[07:29] Marcus Vong: yes we can add configurable network delay distributions to the replay; we'll share the config options.
[07:36] Jordan Lee: can we talk about observability — console will show per-route latency, token breakdown, cost by token bucket, and per-request traces if you enable tracing. We'll also attach trace IDs to benchmark runs so you can map sample input to model outputs.
[07:54] Maya Chen: that's helpful. For compliance we need redaction controls in logs, can you redact sensitive fields pre-ingest?
[08:02] Priya Patel: yes, we support pre-ingest redaction rules; we'll include a template for regex redactions.
[08:10] Tobias Reed: final question on fallback policies — if primary 13B saturates, do you have automated routing to smaller lower-quality models or to a cached response?
[08:20] Priya Patel: we support model-level fallback routing and also can return cached templates for known flows. We can define policy thresholds based on queue depth or latency.
[08:30] Maya Chen: ok, next steps and owners?
[08:33] Jordan Lee: action items we agreed: jordan send runbook; priya send config suggestions and cost deltas; lina export trace; ravi confirm peering windows. We'll reconvene after customer upload.
[08:45] Maya Chen: thanks all, that was productive.
[08:48] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the doc and link to the replay s3.
